client.name: Falaj Community Bank
client.fictional_note: Falaj Community Bank is a fictional bank. Its profile is a composite of a small digital bank in Abu Dhabi; it is not any real institution.

brand.tagline: Banking that flows to the community

facts: App, contact centre and one branch; Arabic and English

rates._note: Illustrative reference market rates in $ per million tokens. Not quotes.

private.label: private open-weight model running in the bank's own infrastructure

agents.name: Shopping concierge
agents.desc: Finds products across partner merchants, compares prices and reviews, applies promo codes and pays in one tap.
agents.control: Never pays without the customer's tap; spending limits are set by the customer.

agents.name: Money co-pilot
agents.desc: Pays bills and subscriptions, flags unused ones, moves spare cash to savings or gold and splits bills.
agents.control: Acts only within customer-set limits; new payees always need confirmation.

agents.name: Life-event journeys
agents.desc: One request, such as moving home, runs rent, utilities, furniture and cover offers as one journey.
agents.control: Every payment or application inside a journey needs the customer's approval.

agents.name: KYC fast-track
agents.desc: Summarises stalled verifications and missing documents so analysts clear them in minutes.

agents.name: SME co-pilot
agents.desc: Payroll (WPS) files, supplier payments and financing offers when cash runs short.

agents.name: SME credit pre-assessment
agents.desc: Collects documents and drafts a credit memo for the credit team.

agents.name: Circular review
agents.desc: Summarises new public regulator circulars for compliance.

addons_extra: Family transfers, complaints handling and an Arabic voice agent.

title: FireFlow at
Falaj Community Bank.
intro.lead: How the FireFlow commercial journey could run for a small digital bank in Abu Dhabi. The bank is fictional; the figures are based on real-world cases and our work with financial institutions.

title: A bank app
used only to pay.
bank.lead: Falaj serves individuals and small businesses through its app and one branch. Like most banks, it is losing its customers' attention to other apps.

items.title: Payments-only app
items.text: Customers open it to check a balance or pay, then leave.

items.title: Invisible at checkout
items.text: Shopping happens on marketplaces; the bank only processes the card.

items.title: Slow to launch
items.text: Every new service waits months in the IT release queue.

gate: One assistant in the Falaj app turns many apps into one journey, and bank teams can build new agents themselves.

title: Three agents first.
More when ready.
use_cases.lead: Stage 1 scopes three customer agents that bring shopping, money and life admin into the Falaj app.

title: One app
instead of three.
before_after.lead: Today a Falaj customer leaves the app to shop and comes back only to pay. With the shopping concierge, the whole purchase happens in the bank app.

before.label: TODAY
steps: Track the order in another app

after.label: WITH FALAJ AND FIREFLOW
steps: Ask: “Air fryer under AED 400, good reviews, by Friday”
Approve one of three options with a tap

gate: The bank owns the moment of purchase: partner commissions, more card spend and a daily reason to open the app.

title: Runs inside the bank.
Controlled by the bank.
systems.lead: FireFlow is installed in the bank's own data centre or private cloud. Bank engineers connect its systems and decide what each agent may do.

items.title: On-premises deployment
items.text: FireFlow and its data stay inside the bank's infrastructure.

items.title: Bank-controlled access
items.text: Bank engineers connect core banking, cards and partner merchants through approved APIs and MCP.

items.title: No vendor access to data
items.text: Persistent Labs works only with synthetic data and never sees bank or customer data.

gate: Customer data and the AI models stay inside the bank; merchants see only orders a customer approves. Persistent Labs has no access.

title: Staging for
three agents.
staging.lead: Persistent Labs sets up an isolated staging environment with synthetic data, trains the bank's business and engineering teams and writes the three agent specifications.
note: Synthetic customer data; no production access.
gate: Staging ready; specifications for all three agents signed off.

title: Build and test
in two languages.
build.lead: Agents are built against sandbox APIs and partner-merchant test catalogues, with Arabic and English test sets agreed with the bank.
gate: All three agents pass the agreed tests; the bank's business and engineering teams can edit the flows.

title: Your product team
builds its own agents.
team.lead: Trained in Stage 1, Falaj product managers assemble new agents in FireFlow's visual builder without code and test them in staging with synthetic data.
note: New agents reach customers only after the bank's controls and approvals.
gate: New services ship without waiting in the IT release queue, built by the people who own the product.

title: Controls before
customers.
prepare.lead: Persistent Labs and the bank agree what each agent may do alone and what needs a person.
gate: Bank infosec and compliance approve the plan; Persistent Labs and the bank test the controls and the emergency stop.

title: Start with
5% of customers.
rollout.lead: The bank's engineers connect production APIs and partner merchants. About 5% of app users get the three agents first.
gate: Expand once compliance has reviewed the audit trail and four weeks have passed without critical incidents.

title: All customers.
Bank in control.
operate.lead: All app users get the three agents. The bank runs operations; Persistent Labs ships updates and support.
split: Updates, fixes and incident support, with no access to customer data.

title: Inference costs
at full volume.
usage.lead: Monthly estimate at full volume. All three agents are customer-facing and run on a private model inside the bank, so 25% applies to a market-rate reference.
gate: Monthly in arrears. The reference is only the basis for the surcharge; the bank's own hardware is not billed again.

title: What could
come next.
addons.lead: Each add-on gets its own statement of work, price and acceptance tests.

title: Year one,
in one view.
year_one.lead: Months 1–12 for the three initial agents. Add-on services are excluded.
